title: Temporal Evidence Forests for Long-Horizon Multi-Party Conversational Memory
abstract: arXiv:2610.12874v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Long-term memory has been widely adopted in LLM-based agents to support persistent interaction and personalized assistance. Long-term multi-party interactions, however, accumulate substantially more detailed information, with decisions repeatedly updated and states evolving across participants and interaction stages. Temporal structure is therefore crucial for tracing such memories: relevant information often appears densely within short intervals, while transitions among different states are anchored by a strict temporal order. Existing temporally aware memory frameworks primarily store time as metadata or use temporal signals to guide retrieval over preconstructed memory structures, without using temporal structure to both recover locally concentrated evidence and reconstruct its complete event progression. translated_title: 面向长程多方对话记忆的时间证据森林
translated_abstract: 长期记忆已被广泛应用于基于大语言模型（LLM）的智能体中，以支持持久交互和个性化辅助。然而，长期的多方交互会积累大量详细信息，其中决策被反复更新，状态在不同参与者和交互阶段之间不断演化。因此，时间结构对于追踪此类记忆至关重要：相关信息往往在短时间间隔内密集出现，而不同状态之间的转换则由严格的时间顺序所锚定。现有的时间感知记忆框架主要将时间作为元数据存储，或使用时间信号来指导对预先构建记忆结构的检索，而未能利用时间结构来同时恢复局部集中的证据并重构其完整的事件演进过程。为解决这些局限，我们提出了T-Mem，一个基于时间结构的记忆框架，该框架保存交互并组织……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出T-Mem——一种基于时间结构的记忆框架，通过“时间证据森林”同时恢复局部时间区间内密集集中的证据并重构完整的事件演进顺序，从而克服现有记忆框架仅将时间作为元数据或检索信号、无法追踪长程多方对话记忆动态演变的局限。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes T-Mem, a temporal-structure-based memory framework using "Temporal Evidence Forests" to both recover locally concentrated evidence within short intervals and reconstruct complete event progressions, addressing the limitation of existing memory frameworks that treat time merely as metadata or retrieval signals for long-horizon multi-party conversational memory.
